candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: U_tau/U_inf is dimensionless. Using the six listed dimensional inputs (U_inf, nu, MKE, delta, delta*, theta) all have known SI dimensional exponents: U_inf [L T^-1], nu [L^2 T^-1], MKE [L^3 T^-2] (integral of velocity squared over wall-normal distance), and the three thicknesses delta, delta*, theta [L]. From these, Buckingham Pi yields dimensionless groups (for example Reynolds numbers based on U_inf and length scales, geometric ratios delta*/delta, theta/delta, and a nondimensional MKE such as MKE/(U_inf^2 delta)). Therefore U_tau/U_inf can be expressed as a function of those dimensionless groups; the dimensional exponents of the inputs are fully known with high confidence.

variables.physical_definition: Magnitude of the free-stream (far-field) fluid velocity relative to the body or wall.
Kinematic viscosity of the fluid (dynamic viscosity divided by density), governing viscous diffusion of momentum.
Integral from the wall to the boundary-layer edge of the square of the local mean velocity (u(y)^2) with respect to wall-normal distance.
Boundary-layer thickness (distance from the wall to the location where local mean velocity reaches 99% of free-stream).
Displacement thickness: the distance by which external streamlines are displaced due to the boundary layer (integral of (1 - u/U_inf) dy).
Momentum thickness: the thickness representing momentum deficit in the boundary layer (integral of (u/U_inf)(1 - u/U_inf) dy).

That record therefore applies directly to the ledger U_inf and supports the exponents I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=-1, Theta=0.

The ledger defines nu as kinematic viscosity (dynamic viscosity divided by density). The KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity gives the canonical definition 'kinematic viscosity' and specifies SI dimensions L^2 T^-1, matching the ledger meaning of nu. This record therefore justifies the exponents I=0, J=0, L=2, M=0, N=0, T=-1, Theta=0 for nu.

The ledger labels MKE as the integral of the square of local mean velocity with respect to wall-normal distance. The KB record pq_integrated_velocity_squared defines this exact integrated-U^2 quantity and states its dimensions follow from U^2 times length, i.e. L^3 T^-2. That entry therefore directly applies to the ledger variable MKE and supports the exponents I=0, J=0, L=3, M=0, N=0, T=-2, Theta=0.

The ledger defines delta as the boundary-layer thickness (99% free-stream). Therefore that record applies to delta* and supports the exponents I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=0, Theta=0.

The ledger names theta as the boundary-layer momentum thickness. Citing pq_momentum_thickness therefore justifies exponents I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=0, Theta=0 for theta.
